post.caption: Found in a shovelful of gravel. In 1893, a worker at the Jagersfontein mine in South Africa spotted the Excelsior Diamond while loading a truck. He skipped his overseer and took it to the mine manager, and he was rewarded with 500 pounds and a saddled horse. The rough stone weighed nearly 1,000 carats. It stayed the biggest diamond known until the Cullinan in 1905. Asscher of Amsterdam began cutting it in 1903 and made 21 polished gems. The biggest, Excelsior I, is a pear shape of about 70 carats.
